les: Hoekom lyk die Maan elke aand anders
kaps_punt: Fases van die Maan - die Son se lig skyn op die oppervlak van die Maan; ons kan net die deel van die Maan sien waarop die Son skyn; die veranderende patroon van sonlig op die Maan word die fases van die Maan genoem; die patroon herhaal elke 29 en 'n half dae (ongeveer 'n maand)

items.bewering: Kyk een aand na die Maan, en dit lyk asof dit self brand.
items.blok: Die Maan maak nie sy eie lig nie
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases (science.nasa.gov/moon/moon-phases): 'The Moon does not make its own light. Moonlight is actually reflected sunlight.' This sentence is an impression ('lyk asof'), and the next sentence corrects it at once. The mapping cannot leave a learner believing the Moon burns. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Anders as die Son maak die Maan egter nie sy eie lig nie.
items.blok: Die Maan maak nie sy eie lig nie
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: 'The Moon does not make its own light.' The Sun is the light source in the same explanation. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Son se lig val op die Maan se oppervlak. Dit is daardie sonlig wat ons van die Aarde af sien.
items.blok: Die Maan maak nie sy eie lig nie
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: 'Moonlight is actually reflected sunlight.' Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Sonder die lig van die Son sou die Maan vir ons donker wees.
items.blok: Die Maan maak nie sy eie lig nie
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases (the Moon makes no light of its own). Earthshine also lights the Moon faintly, but earthshine is sunlight reflected by the Earth, so the claim holds. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Son skyn heeltyd op een helfte van die Maan. Daardie helfte is vol lig, en die ander helfte kry op daardie oomblik geen sonlig nie.
items.blok: Die Son skyn op een helfte
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: 'The Moon is always half-lit by the Sun.' NASA Space Place, Moon phases: 'The Sun always illuminates half of the Moon while the other half remains dark.' Lunar eclipses are the only exception to 'heeltyd'. Even then the Moon is lit dimly by sunlight bent through Earth's atmosphere (timeanddate.com, why the Moon looks red in a lunar eclipse). Eclipses are outside this bullet and do not mislead about phases. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Dit is nie altyd dieselfde helfte wat die lig kry nie. Elke kant van die Maan kry ook later sy beurt in die Son se lig.
items.blok: Die Son skyn op een helfte
items.bron: BBC Sky at Night Magazine, 'Dark side of the Moon? There's no such thing': each hemisphere has about two weeks of sunlight and two weeks of darkness every lunar month, and the far side is fully sunlit at new moon. NASA Space Place: 'At new moon, the far side of the Moon is facing the Sun.' Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Op die meeste aande sien ons van die Aarde af nie die hele verligte helfte nie.
items.blok: Die Son skyn op een helfte
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: we see the whole lit half only around full moon. At every other phase we see part of it, for example 'half of its illuminated side' at first quarter. So 'die meeste aande' is accurate, and it is the lesson's only superlative form. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Ons sien net die deel daarvan wat na ons toe wys. Die res van die verligte helfte wys weg van ons, na die ruimte toe.
items.blok: Die Son skyn op een helfte
items.bron: NASA Space Place, Moon phases: how much of the lit half we can see depends on where the Moon is in its orbit. NASA Science, Moon Phases says the same. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Maan bly nie op een plek naby die Aarde nie. Dit volg heeltyd 'n groot pad om die Aarde. Daardie pad om die Aarde word 'n wentelbaan genoem.
items.blok: Hoekom ons uitsig elke aand verander
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases (the Moon's orbit carries it around Earth). NASA's article for young readers defines an orbit as 'a curved path ... that something follows as it goes around an object in space' (nasa.gov). Calling the orbit a 'pad' holds up: a learner who reasons further from it reaches a route the Moon keeps following, which is correct. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Elke aand is die Maan dus op 'n ander plek om die Aarde. Ons kyk elke aand uit 'n ander rigting na die verligte helfte. Daarom sien ons elke aand 'n ander deel van daardie helfte.
items.blok: Hoekom ons uitsig elke aand verander
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: the waxing crescent 'grows daily as the Moon's orbit carries the Moon's dayside farther into view'. The mechanism is the changing Sun-Earth-Moon viewing angle, not Earth's shadow, and the lesson says nothing about a shadow. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Maan bly heeltyd ewe groot, en die Son se lig bly ewe sterk. Net ons uitsig op die verligte helfte verander.
items.blok: Hoekom ons uitsig elke aand verander
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: phases come from the viewing angle alone. The Moon's real size does not change. Its apparent size changes with distance (a 'supermoon' looks up to 14% larger than a full moon at apogee, Smithsonian Magazine quoting NASA), but the sentence is about the Moon itself and is true. Read in context, 'ewe sterk' means the light does not dim to make the phases, which is correct. The lunar-eclipse exception is noted under 'Die Son skyn heeltyd'. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Party aande sien ons niks van die Maan se verligte helfte nie. Daardie tyd noem ons nuwemaan, en hier begin die patroon.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: at new moon the lit side faces away from Earth and the Moon 'rises and sets with the Sun', so we cannot see it. timeanddate.com, Lunar month, and Wikipedia, New moon: a lunation runs from one new moon to the next. 'Hier begin die patroon' follows the astronomical convention. Some calendars count from the first crescent instead, but the lesson presents no competing count. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Maan is nie weg nie; ons kan net nie die verligte helfte sien nie.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: at new moon the Moon is still there, with its lit side 'facing away from the Earth'. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Kort daarna sien ons 'n dun boog van lig, en dit is 'n sekelmaan. Die boog word elke aand 'n bietjie breër.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: EarthSky, Waxing crescent (earthsky.org/moon-phases/waxing-crescent): a slim crescent appears in the day or so after every new moon. NASA Science, Moon Phases: the waxing crescent 'grows daily'. af.wikipedia, Maanfase, gives 'sekelmaan' for the crescent. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Later sien ons 'n halwe sirkel van lig, en dit is halfmaan. Die rand van die lig lyk dan amper soos 'n reguit lyn.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: EarthSky, 'Is it a quarter or a half moon?': at the exact first quarter the terminator is straight, and just before or after it curves slightly, so 'amper' is accurate. NASA Science: at first quarter 'you see half of its illuminated side'. af.wikipedia, Maanfase: 'Die term halfmaan word dikwels vir die eerste en laaste kwartier gebruik.' The formal names are eerste and laaste kwartier, but 'halfmaan' is established Afrikaans usage. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Nog later sien ons 'n vol ronde sirkel, en dit is volmaan. Dan wys die hele verligte helfte van die Maan na ons toe.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases (full moon: the whole lit side faces Earth, and it rises around sunset). af.wikipedia, Maanfase: volmaan, 'Skyf heeltemal verlig'. The gibbous phases (bolmaan) between halfmaan and volmaan go unnamed, but nothing says there is nothing in between, so that is an omission and not an error. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Daarna sien ons weer 'n halwe sirkel en later weer 'n dun boog.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: after full moon come the waning gibbous, the third (last) quarter and the waning crescent, then new moon again. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die Maan beweeg heeltyd in dieselfde rigting. Net die vorms wat ons sien, verander totdat dit weer nuwemaan is.
items.blok: Die vorms van nuwemaan tot volmaan en weer terug
items.bron: University of Oregon astronomy course page, 'Recall the moon's orbit' (pages.uoregon.edu/soper/Orbits/moonorbit2.html): the Moon orbits Earth counterclockwise as seen from the north. The orbit is prograde and never reverses. This rightly heads off the idea that the Moon turns back after full moon. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Al hierdie veranderende vorms word saam die fases van die Maan genoem.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases. af.wikipedia, Maanfase. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Begin op 'n aand wanneer jy 'n dun boog laag in die weste sien. Kyk elke aand kort na sononder en nie teen slaaptyd nie.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: EarthSky, Waxing crescent, and EarthSky 'Young moon low in west after sunset': the young crescent is in the west shortly after sunset and 'quickly follows the sun below the western horizon', so 'not at bedtime' is sound advice. The west-after-sunset position comes from the Moon being close to the Sun, so it holds in the Southern Hemisphere too. The lesson does not say which side of the Moon is lit, which would differ between hemispheres. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Skryf die vorm neer, en jy sien hoe dit aand na aand groter word.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: the waxing crescent 'grows daily', and the waxing phases are seen in the evening. The first quarter 'rises around midday' and the full moon 'rises around sunset', so the Moon is up after sunset all through the waxing half. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Later kom die Maan eers laat in die nag op. Kyk dan vroeg in die oggend, en jy sien hoe die stuk lig weer kleiner word.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: the waning gibbous 'rises later and later each night', and the waning crescent 'rises in the very early morning, before sunrise'. Wikipedia, Moonrise and moonset: last quarter rises around midnight, and moonrise comes about 50 minutes later each day on average. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Na omtrent 'n maand is die vorm weer soos aan die begin.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: 'The cycle repeats about once a month (every 29.5 days).' Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die hele patroon van vorms herhaal hom elke 29 en 'n half dae.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: Wikipedia, Month: the mean synodic month is 29.53059 days. NASA Science: 'every 29.5 days'. timeanddate.com, Lunar month: single cycles vary from about 29.26 to 29.80 days, so the figure is an average. It is the CAPS figure and correct as a Grade 4 average. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Dit is omtrent so lank soos 'n maand op die kalender. Die maande op 'n kalender is nie almal ewe lank nie.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: timeanddate.com, Months of the year (timeanddate.com/calendar/months): Gregorian months have 28 to 31 days (seven of 31, four of 30, and February with 28 or 29). Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Jy hoef ook nie net snags te kyk nie. Die Maan is op party dae ook bedags sigbaar.
items.blok: Die patroon herhaal homself
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: the Moon is 'often visible during the day as a faint, pale presence'. Live Science, 'Daytime moon': it is visible in daylight on most days of the month, but not near new moon or full moon, so 'op party dae' is accurate. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: fase: Een van die vorms waarin ons die Maan van die Aarde af sien.
items.blok: begrip: fase
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases (phases are the shapes of the lit part we see from Earth). af.wikipedia, Maanfase. Read alone, the entry is accurate and does not suggest the Moon itself changes shape. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: nuwemaan: Die tyd wanneer die Maan se verligte helfte heeltemal weg van die Aarde wys.
items.blok: begrip: nuwemaan
items.bron: NASA Science, Moon Phases: at new moon the lit side is 'facing away from the Earth'. NASA Space Place: 'At new moon, the far side of the Moon is facing the Sun.' 'Heeltemal' is exact only when the alignment is perfect, but it is accurate at Grade 4 because nothing lit can be seen. af.wikipedia, Maanfase, calls this phase 'donkermaan'. That is the same phase under another name, not a contradiction. Read alone and in its block, the entry is correct. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: sekelmaan: Die Maan wanneer ons 'n boog van lig sien wat kleiner as 'n halwe sirkel is.
items.blok: begrip: sekelmaan
items.bron: Farmers' Almanac, Learn the Moon Phases, and Dictionary.com (gibbous): a crescent is lit to less than one half, and a gibbous moon to more than one half. af.wikipedia, Maanfase: sekelmaan, as opposed to bolmaan. Read alone, it covers waxing and waning crescents, which is correct. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: halfmaan: Die Maan wanneer ons 'n halwe sirkel van lig sien.
items.blok: begrip: halfmaan
items.bron: af.wikipedia, Maanfase: 'halfmaan' is often used for first and last quarter. EarthSky: at quarter phase about half the disc is lit. Read alone, the entry is correct. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: volmaan: Die Maan wanneer ons 'n vol ronde sirkel van lig sien.
items.blok: begrip: volmaan
items.bron: af.wikipedia, Maanfase: volmaan, 'Skyf heeltemal verlig'. NASA Science, Moon Phases. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: wentelbaan: Die pad waarlangs een ding om 'n ander ding beweeg.
items.blok: begrip: wentelbaan
items.bron: NASA (nasa.gov, article on orbits for young readers): an orbit is 'a curved path ... that something follows as it goes around an object in space'. The lesson's entry is correct for the Moon and Earth. Read alone, it is broader than the astronomical sense, because it leaves out 'in die ruimte', so a track around a field would also fit. That makes it imprecise but not false at Grade 4. Recorded so a person can decide whether to narrow it. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: oppervlak: Die hele buitekant van 'n ding.
items.blok: begrip: oppervlak
items.bron: Dictionary.com, surface: 'the outer face, outside, or exterior boundary of a thing'. Oxford Learner's Dictionaries: 'the outside or top layer of something'. Read alone, and next to block 2 ('Die Son skyn ... op een helfte'), it does not suggest the Sun lights the whole surface at once. Checked in full this round.

opsomming: Every claim was checked in full this round against NASA, EarthSky, timeanddate.com, Afrikaans Wikipedia and standard dictionaries, and none was contradicted or left uncertain; the lesson has no superlative except 'op die meeste aande', which is true, and the one point a person may want to look at is a matter of precision, not truth: read alone, the 'wentelbaan' entry leaves out 'in die ruimte' and so is broader than the astronomical sense.
